Nora (CSM): FYI flagged: Aurora Labs renewal tagged high-risk in this morning's run. Active integrations down ~58% over 11 days. Their champion (C. Vega) moved to data platform. Need quick triage.
Sam (AM): Oof. Any error spikes or just quiet?
Nora (CSM): Quiet mostly. A handful of 5xxs ~3 weeks ago that were patched. Usage fall appears across transform routes, embeddings slightly less affected.
Diego (SE): Can you paste the route-level query you ran? Ill pull telemetry and check KV/cache & routing.
Nora (CSM): SQL I used:
```sql
SELECT route, date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, count(*) as calls
FROM requests
WHERE customer_id='auroralabs' AND ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```
Nora (CSM): Top days: 2026-02-26: 1,040; 2026-03-05: 420; 2026-03-07: 360.
billing-bot: Notice: invoice #A-9812 has an outstanding dispute opened 2026-03-06 by Aurora Labs (reason: unexpected tokens).
Priya (Solutions Eng): Could be client-side key rotation or a new integration path. Also procurement wrote a note about a competitor POC last week.
Sam (AM): Yup, procurement flagged "evaluating alternate vendor" in call notes. Likely active scouting.
Diego (SE): Running quick telemetry now. If client rotated keys we'd see many 401s followed by silence; if cache invalidation we'd see many small single-token calls. Give me 20m.
Nora (CSM): I've DM'd Aurora's new contact (L. Huang) to announce we'll reach out with an offer.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Suggestion: offer a 10-day no-cost pilot cluster + 1:1 onboarding for the new ML lead and a short technical health-check. Historically reduces churn when migration/misconfig is root cause.
Sam (AM): Also prepare a commercial play: trial extension + a limited credit vs competitor pricing if they show a valid POC spec.
Diego (SE): Quick findings: no server-side fallbacks or latency regressions. But KV cache hit rate dropped from ~74% -> 14% between 2026-02-26 and 2026-03-07. Also a burst of tiny requests (median tokens/request = 3). Likely client-side change.
Nora (CSM): that matches their billing dispute comment (unexpected token usage). I'll raise this on the call and offer the sandbox + enablement.
Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a 30-min session for the new ML lead: batching, context reuse, and embed pooling. Deck ETA 18h.
Sam (AM): I'll update CRM: tag = "advocate-moved"; play = "pilot+workshop"; and queue a 30m QBR with dev + procurement.
Nora (CSM): Draft outreach I'll send: "We saw a drop in transform traffic and a rise in small calls. Would you be open to a short sandbox + pairing session to verify SDK behavior and reduce token spend? We can also pause billing dispute while we investigate." Thoughts?
Sam (AM): good. Add a request for a short POC spec if procurement is evaluating rivals (3 acceptance metrics). We'll offer credits if they commit to the POC.
Diego (SE): Runbook snippet for customer: `curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq '.latency.p50, .latency.p95'` and capture 5 consecutive samples; include 3 request IDs from /v1/transform.
Nora (CSM): Actions: 1) Diego full log audit and attach sample request IDs (ETA 2h). 2) Priya workshop prep (ETA 18h). 3) Sam update CRM, add play & schedule QBR (ETA 24h). 4) Nora outreach + billing pause request (ASAP).
Diego (SE): Follow-up: found one client pattern where the SDK was instantiating new sessions per request and not reusing the batch key. I'll paste a sanitized example in the audit.
Nora (CSM): great catch. That explains both the token spike and the dispute. I'll call L. Huang now and push the sandbox + pairing session. Will update here. :thumbsup:
